document.title: UFOs regularly spotted in restricted U.S. airspace, report on the phenomena due next month (60 Minutes)
document.author: Bill Whitaker

passages.text: Bill Whitaker: So what you are telling me is that UFOs, unidentified flying objects, are real?
Lue Elizondo: Bill, I think we're beyond that already. The government has already stated for the record that they're real. I'm not telling you that. The United States government is telling you that.

document.title: U.S. military tested device that may be tied to Havana Syndrome on rats, sheep, confidential sources say (60 Minutes)
document.author: Scott Pelley

passages.text: Former CIA officer: So one of the very first things that I heard when I arrived at the AHI Unit was, "Our job is to bring down the temperature on AHI at headquarters." And that was a surprise to me. So bringing down the temperature is not, "Hey, let's go after the issue and find out what's going on." It became very much a emotional and almost kind of like a propaganda type thing.
All of this, he says, led him to resign.

quotes.quote: So one of the very first things that I heard when I arrived at the AHI Unit was, "Our job is to bring down the temperature on AHI at headquarters."
All of this, he says, led him to resign.

differs: The teller does not say which 60 Minutes report he means; if it is the 60 Minutes report on Havana Syndrome of 8 March 2026, a former CIA officer who resigned says that when he arrived at the CIA's unit for anomalous health incidents (Havana Syndrome) he heard "Our job is to bring down the temperature on AHI at headquarters"; the report does not say who said it or that it was a woman, and its subject is Havana Syndrome, not UFOs. The 60 Minutes UFO report of May 2021 holds no such line.

document.title: Elite Officer Recalls Bin Laden Hunt (60 Minutes)
document.author: Scott Pelley

passages.text: But they didn't take that route, because Fury says they didn't get approval from a higher level. "Whether that was Central Command all the way up to the president of the United States, I'm not sure," he says.
But they didn't do that either, because Fury says that plan was also disapproved. He says he has "no idea" why.

The military wouldn't tell 60 Minutes who rejected the plans or why. Fury wasn't happy about it but he pressed on with the only option he had left, a frontal assault on bin Laden's dug-in al Qaeda fighters. The Delta team had only about 50 men. So the mission would depend on the Afghan militia as guides and muscle. Their leader was a warlord and self-styled general named Ali.

It was night, so Fury was without his Afghan allies. Still, he rescued his men and then found himself approaching bin Laden's doorstep. "We're about 2,000 meters away from where we think bin Laden's at still. From where we're at. Now we have to make a decision," he remembers.

Asked why he feels that way, Fury says, "Had we gone up that ridgeline towards that location, Osama bin Laden might have been 500 meters way. We might have run right into him. So there's always that doubt that we might have run into him. We also might got up there and found nothing. It wasn't worth the risk at that particular moment to go up there and play cowboy. It was better to be cautious, refit, go up there with the entire force the next day and play the battle out as we had planned."

quotes.quote: But they didn't take that route, because Fury says they didn't get approval from a higher level.
But they didn't do that either, because Fury says that plan was also disapproved.
The military wouldn't tell 60 Minutes who rejected the plans or why.
We're about 2,000 meters away from where we think bin Laden's at still.
It wasn't worth the risk at that particular moment to go up there and play cowboy.

differs: In the 60 Minutes report of October 2008, Dalton Fury says two of Delta's plans against bin Laden at Tora Bora (coming over the mountains from the Pakistan side, and mining the passes into Pakistan) were disapproved by higher headquarters; the report does not speak of having bin Laden in sight three times or of overwatch, and it says that on the night his team was about 2,000 meters from where they thought bin Laden was, Fury himself decided not to advance.
